subject: Aligning FY calendar + staged consumption credits for upcoming renewal
messages:
From: Alicia Turner <alicia.turner@novus.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procure@novus.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal timing + fiscal alignment?

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the Q4 usage recap — really helpful. Our finance team is pushing to align supplier contracts with our fiscal year (starts 4/1 for us). We have an upcoming renewal anniversary in mid-May and would like to: 

- Move the renewal to 4/1 co-term with FY start (short pro-rated period is ok)
- Stage consumption credits to smooth invoice impact (we expect a big ramp in Q3)
- Keep the unit pricing stable but request a small backloaded credit structure tied to consumption buckets

Can Redwood put together a proposed cadence and credit schedule that both aligns to calendar and avoids a large Q2 invoice hit? Procurement is looped (procure@novus.ai) — happy to set up a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Turner
Head of Platform Ops, Novus AI
Alicia.turner@novus.ai

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com

Cc: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + fiscal alignment?

Hi Alicia —

Appreciate the clear ask. We can absolutely align the renewal to your FY start and design staged consumption credits to smooth Q2/Q3. High level proposal below — attaching a first-pass SOW and a usage projection workbook.

High-level proposal:
- Term: 3/30/28–3/31/31 (3-year) co-term effective 4/1/28 with a 2-week pro-rate period (invoiced as credit note).
- Staged credits: 20% credit against overage tokens in Q1 (4/1–6/30) to smooth onboarding, 10% in Q2, then standard pricing thereafter; alternative: backloaded credit of 30% applied as invoice credit over Q3–Q4 if consumption milestones met.
- Ramp schedule: baseline commit of 250K token units/month for first 6 months, stepped to 500K months 7–12, then 1M thereafter. The attached spreadsheet models both linear and backloaded consumption curves.

Questions for procurement:
- Do you need invoice cadence matched to your fiscal quarters, or is monthly billing with quarterly credits acceptable?
- Any legal/PO timing constraints for DocuSign execution?

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal pricing confirmation (Ben / Priya) — can you confirm margin-friendly credit buckets?
2) Quick call with Alicia + procurement to confirm cadence (30 min) — propose Thu 2/17 10am PT.
3) Finalize SOW + send DocuSign link for signature.

Attachments: SOW_Novus_Q1_v2.pdf, novus_usage_projection_v3.xlsx

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0142

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 08:29:00 -08:00
Subject: FW: Renewal timing + fiscal alignment? (pricing ask)

Ben / Steph / Priya —

Looping you in for pricing approval and margin checks. Novus is asking for calendar alignment to 4/1 and a couple of credit structures we can choose from. Quick ask: which of the two below is acceptable from a pricing and operational perspective? We need to confirm before the Thu call with procurement.

Option A — Smoothing credits (recommended operationally)
- 20% credit on overage tokens Q1; 10% Q2
- Baseline commit: 250K token units/mo first 6 months, then step-up to 500K/mo months 7–12
- Standard SLA; no additional enterprise discount
- Expected revenue recognition: pro-rate into Q2 (small hit)

Option B — Backloaded rebate (better for Novus finance)
- 30% credit applied as invoice rebate across Q3–Q4 contingent on hitting 120% of baseline commit in months 7–9
- Baseline commit: 300K token units/mo first 3 months, then aggressive step-up
- Requires longer term (36 months) to protect unit economics

Quick notes: the attached usage model shows cashflow difference between options. For co-terming we will do a short pro-rate invoiced as credit rather than a complicated amendment.

Please reply with preference or edits by 12pm PT today so I can present on the call.

—Marissa

From: Alicia Turner <alicia.turner@novus.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Novus AI Procurement <procure@novus.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Feb 2028 10:11:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + fiscal alignment?

Marissa —

Thanks, the plan looks reasonable. Procurement prefers Option B (backloaded rebate) because it lets us defer hit into later quarters and ties credits to consumption milestones. A few clarifications: 

- We need monthly invoices, but rebates can post quarterly.
- DocuSign needs to be received by 3/15 to meet PO cycle — can you confirm timeline?
- Can you add an explicit clause for early-exit true-up if we miss the consumption milestone in year 2?

If you can send a DocuSign link with Option B and the early-exit true-up language, procurement will review and route for signature. Happy to take the 2/24 slot if you want to review final redlines.

Best,
Alicia
